data.content:
Philemon
Philemon is the husband of Baucis, who together with her, showed hospitality to Zeus and Hermes.

Slaves
Slaves are the individuals that Demeter sends away before punishing Erysichthon.

Demeter
Demeter is the goddess who punishes Erysichthon with a curse for his actions.<SEP>Demeter is the goddess of agriculture, connected to a sacred oak tree and associated with Erysichthon's punishment.

Baucis
Baucis is a poor, elderly woman who, along with her husband Philemon, shown kindness to Zeus and Hermes by offering them food and shelter.

Athena
Athena is a goddess who offered to turn Paris into a courageous soldier in the contest for the golden apple.<SEP>Athena is the daughter of Zeus, characterized as strong and wise, known for offering the olive tree as a gift to the citizens of a new city.

Aphrodite
Aphrodite is the goddess of love, known for her beauty and involvement in starting a war inadvertently.<SEP>Aphrodite is the goddess of love, associated with beauty and the origin of a war due to a golden apple.

Apollo
Apollo is the twin brother of Artemis and one of the major gods of Olympus.<SEP>Apollo is one of the gods whose cattle was stolen by Hermes; he is enchanted by Hermes' music played on the lyre.

The City of Athens
The City of Athens is a city named after Athena, chosen by the citizens for protection due to her gift of the olive tree.

Ares
Ares is the god of war, known for his lack of loyalty in battle and a relationship with Aphrodite, influencing his actions during the Trojan War.

Poseidon
Poseidon is the god of the seas and a rival of Athena, known for providing a river as a gift to a new city.

Zeus
Zeus is the god of the sky and ruler of the gods, known for traveling with his son, Hermes, and meting out justice to those who refused him hospitality.

Hera
Hera is a goddess who believed she was the fairest and participated in the contest for the golden apple.

Helen
Helen is described as the most beautiful woman in the world, married to the king of Sparta and central to the Trojan War.

Paris
Paris is a mortal chosen to decide who should own the golden apple among the goddesses.

The Curse
The curse placed on Erysichthon is that his hunger would never be satisfied, leading to his perpetual suffering.

Erysichthon
Erysichthon is a character who faced punishment from the goddess Demeter for his insatiable hunger.<SEP>Erysichthon is depicted as arrogant and greedy, responsible for the destruction of a sacred tree dedicated to Demeter.

Hermes
Hermes is the son of Zeus, known for his cleverness and mischievous nature, who created the lyre and served as a messenger between gods and mortals.

Eris
Eris is the goddess who enjoys being a troublemaker and created a golden apple that instigated a conflict among goddesses.<SEP>Eris is the goddess of discord, known for causing conflict among goddesses by creating the Golden Apple.

Golden Apple
The Golden Apple is a significant object in the story, inscribed with 'For the fairest,' leading to conflict among the goddesses Hera, Aphrodite, and Athena.

Orpheus
Orpheus is a singer who traveled to the Underworld to retrieve his deceased wife and enchanted Hades with his singing.

Trojan War
The Trojan War is a significant conflict lasting ten years that began due to Helen's elopement with Paris.

Dionysus
Dionysus is the god of wine who was asked by the gods to intoxicate Hephaestus to free Hera.

Hephaestus
Hephaestus is the son of Hera known for creating a golden throne as revenge on his mother.

Artemis
Artemis is the goddess of hunting and the moon, depicted as a skilled fighter and hunter.

Hestia
Hestia is the oldest goddess of Olympus, tasked with overseeing the gods' needs and often associated with the home.

Hades
Hades is the god who rules the Underworld and is responsible for ensuring the dead remain there permanently.

Mount Olympus
Mount Olympus is the dwelling place of the gods, including Hera and Hephaestus, where significant events take place.

Alpheus
Alpheus is the river god who fell in love with Artemis and pursued her through the forest.

Underworld
Hades rules the Underworld, the realm of the dead.
